# ms: # One TUI turn in a Sidecar-managed shell, from process start to turn end, with
# a Bash tool call that needed approval. This is the whole ladder Herdr's twelve
# SessionStart carries source=startup and a session_id, so the conversation is
# identifiable. UserPromptSubmit is work start. PreToolUse carries tool_name, so
# the two complementary matchers upstream installs are evaluable. Then the two
# events that make the blocked lane first-class rather than inferred:
# PermissionRequest is the last event before the pane blocks, and
# PermissionResult fires on approval AND on denial -- it carries a `decision`
# field, recorded here as a name only -- so a Kimi pane cannot latch on blocked
# the way a Claude pane does. That single fact is why the blocked lane is
# TurnStarted appears between UserPromptSubmit and the first tool call and is
# NOT hooked by the port: upstream's table does not use it, and it would report
# working a second time for a lane UserPromptSubmit has already opened.
